newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso gets boost from inflows.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso gets boost from inflows.

text.p: The Philippine peso was boosted on Tuesday by dollar inflows for fixed income instruments as well as equity investments, traders said.
It ended at 26.373 from 26.379, with volume higher at $263.4 million from $261.5 million.
The inflows, which started shortly before midday, prodded the Philippine Central Bank to adjust its offer rate for the dollar back to 26.375 from 26.379 early in the day, one trader said.
Despite the inflows, the Central Bank was not seen buying dollars. "They (the Central Bank) were just quoting," a trader said, to give an indication where it wanted the peso to trade.
Traders said the peso could move sideways on Wednesday because it could be pulled down by arbitrage play due to the holiday on Thursday.
Manila's financial markets are closed on Thursday for the Philippine Independence Day.
But some traders said the effect of the arbitrage could be offset if the dollar inflows continued.
"If there will be inflows, there could be (dollar) buying by the Central Bank to replenish the dollars it sold in recent days," a trader said.
